output_json.patch_notes: PropertyClass.fromString now calls Class.forName(v, false, loader) using the thread context classloader (falling back to the class's own loader). initialize=false prevents static-initializer execution, which is the code-execution sink the POV exploited. The returned Class<?> is identical to before for legitimate uses (e.g. asString() reads value.getName()); initialization still occurs naturally if/when the class is actually instantiated or used by the application, matching normal JVM lazy-init semantics. Verified: the validated POV (bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh) now prints "NOT VULNERABLE: no attacker code executed." and exits 1; existing PropertyClass tests (tesInitPropertyClass, tesInitPropertyClass2) plus the new regression test tesPropertyClassFromStringDoesNotInitialize all pass.
output_json.risk_notes: Minimal behavior change: any code that previously relied on fromString() eagerly running a class's static initializer would no longer see that side effect at resolution time. This is an unusual and unsafe dependency; standard usage retrieves the Class token and initializes it later on first real use, which is unchanged. An allowlist was considered but rejected because PropertyClass is designed to hold arbitrary user-configured class names, so an allowlist would break legitimate functionality; disabling initialization is the smallest fix that blocks the RCE while preserving intended behavior.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-094 code injection in PropertyClass.fromString(). The method passed untrusted input to the single-argument Class.forName(v), which loads AND initializes the named class, executing an attacker-controlled static initializer (RCE). Changed it to Class.forName(v, false, loader) so the class token is still resolved for legitimate use but the target class is never initialized, so no attacker static-init code runs. Added a regression test asserting fromString returns the correct class token without triggering the target class's static initializer.
